newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul execution a lesson for others, say Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Kabul execution a lesson for others, say Taleban.

text.p: A man was executed in the grounds of a high school in Kabul on Wednesday for murdering a mother and three small children, the capital's first public execution since the Islamic Taleban took control in September.
Ghulam Mohammed was shot on the playing field of the Amani High School at 3.30 p.m. (1100 GMT), watched by a crowd of about 3,000.
Ghulam was taken to the soccer field in a white pick-up truck flying the Taleban's trademark white flag.
A Taleban cleric addressed the crowd from a loudspeaker truck before the execution took place. "He is being punished according to the law of Islam. Let this be a lesson for others," he said.
The executioner was the father of the family Ghulam was accused of murdering.
Mohammed Alif was handed a Kalashnikov assault rifle by a nearby Taleban. He dropped to one knee and fired a two-second burst of automatic fire at the condemned man.
He then walked over to the prostrate victim and fired another burst into his chest.
In Islamic law, the family of a murder victim has the right to execute the murderer.
Ghulam was convicted of murdering Mohammed Alif's wife and three children during a burglary in December last year.
The Taleban took control of Kabul in late September and now control 75 per cent of the country. They have imposed their strict vision of Islamic law on the parts of the country they control.
One of their first acts was to kill former president Najibullah and his brother, whose bodies were left to hang from a concrete traffic post outside the presidential palace in Kabul.
